text:
B: Hiya, can you hear me alright? I'm Craig.
A: Hiya! Yeah, I can hear you, I'm Gemma. Ooh, is that a cockapoo tail I can see at the bottom there?
B: (laughs) Yeah, that's Biscuit. He's under the table waiting for something to drop.
A: Shut up. Mine's called Biscuit! Cockapoo as well!
B: You're joking. Honestly?
A: I swear to God. He's chewed through my phone charger twice this month. Is it a cockapoo thing, the chewing?
B: Ours ate a sock last week. Whole thing. Kerry was on the phone to the vet at ten at night, I was stood there with a torch in the garden waiting for it to, you know, come out the other end.
A: Oh no! Did it?
B: It did, eventually. Best news I'd had all week, sad to say. So where are you based?
A: Beeston, near Nottingham. I grew up in Derby though, so I'm sort of East Midlands through and through. You?
B: Warrington. Born and bred. Wolves fan, before you ask about the magnet.
A: I wasn't going to, but go on then. What do you do?
B: I'm in sales, commercial flooring. Carpet tiles, vinyl, that sort of thing, for offices, schools, care homes. I cover Cheshire, Merseyside and Greater Manchester, so I basically live on the M62. Did over three hundred miles this week. What about you?
A: I'm a physio. Musculoskeletal, in an NHS outpatient department in Nottingham, and I do sports massage on the side on Saturdays, private clients.
B: A physio! Right, I've got a question for you, then.
A: Go on, everyone does. Is it your back?
B: Ankle. I play five-a-side on a Wednesday, well, I used to play properly, now I sort of hobble about. Turned it a couple of years back and it's never been the same.
A: Did you ever get it looked at? Properly, I mean, not just a bag of peas.
B: Er, does a bag of peas not count? (laughs) No, I never did. I just strap it and crack on.
A: See, that's what everyone does. It's probably weak round the joint now, so it keeps going. You'd want some balance work, standing on one leg while you brush your teeth, that sort of thing. Honestly, it makes a massive difference. I've had people come in on crutches basically and be back playing in a few months.
B: Standing on one leg brushing me teeth. Alfie would love that, he'd be copying me.
A: How old's Alfie?
B: Six. He's just got on the school football team, so he thinks he's Mo Salah now. I'm trying to get to his matches but with work, you know, it's hard.
A: Aww. That must be nice though, watching him. We haven't got kids yet, just the dog and a lodger, which is sort of like a kid who pays rent and leaves the hob on.
B: (laughs) That's not far off a kid, to be fair.
A: Honestly, I came down this morning and the hob was on, no pan, nothing. Dan just looked at me like, don't. Anyway, sorry, I keep going on. Do you like the sales stuff?
B: Yeah, I do, I'm a people person, sort of thing. And there's a car with it, which helps. I'm deciding on the next lease now actually, it's a big decision in our house.
A: Oh, what are you thinking?
B: Kerry wants something sensible, I want something with heated seats, so...
